_note: Recurring AI presenter cast for Active AI. One account, three faces. Appearance fields are placeholders until the real Higgsfield avatars are generated and described. Every prompt with usage='ai-presenter' names one of these ids, so camera/behaviour/disclosure stay identical across appearances -- which is what makes a face recognizable rather than just consistent.
_familiarity_math: At ~5 posts/week across 3 presenters, each face appears ~1.7x/week. That is the minimum cadence where viewers start recognizing someone. Adding a 4th or 5th presenter before posting volume rises would drop each below once a week and defeat the purpose.

shared_direction.camera: Handheld, phone at arm's length — 18–20 inches from the face, at eye level, never angled up or down. Framed chest-up: top of frame ~2 inches above the head, bottom at sternum. No zoom, no push-in, no deliberate movement — only natural handheld micro-shake, not a gimbal glide. Direct eye contact with the lens by default.
shared_direction.behaviour: Eyebrows relaxed and neutral — not the raised 'presenting to camera' default that generation tools produce. Mouth soft between sentences, never held in a static smile. No hand gestures for emphasis beyond what a specific prompt calls for.
shared_direction.pacing: Target ~140 wpm, conversational. Maximum gap between sentences 0.4 seconds — added silence is what makes generated output run long and feel unnatural.
shared_direction.disclosure: Every video carries on-screen text identifying the presenter as AI-generated, legible, within the first 3 seconds, held 2 seconds. This is not optional and not a stylistic choice.

compliance_rule: AI presenters perform demonstration scripts only — second person, present tense, about what the app does. They may never make a first-person claim of having used the app, gotten a result from it, or formed an opinion of it. Those are testimonials, and a testimonial from someone who does not exist is prohibited outright, with or without disclosure. Prompts tagged usage='real-creator-only' are for real people who actually use the app, with an #ad disclosure — never for this cast.
_source_image_issues: Both base images are FULL-BODY or mid-torso. Speak lipsync wants a clear front-facing head-and-shoulders frame. Regenerate each as a chest-up portrait, eyes to lens, before using them as input_image.
Fox V1 is a mirror selfie with a phone held up covering part of the face, and her gaze is off-lens. Unusable as a lipsync base as-is.
Fox V1 and Fox V2 are byte-identical duplicates — there is no second variant.
Neither fills the P3 slot (30s-40s female), which carries 8 of the 24 prompts.
_styling_conflict: Both avatars are styled as fashion/lifestyle influencers — designer-look accessories, gold jewellery, considered outfits, polished settings. The prompt library specifies the opposite throughout: "unstyled", "no makeup", "genuinely just-woke-up", "gym-casual", "normal at-home clothes", "not styled for camera". These two directions contradict each other and one of them has to give. See the note in the hub before generating at volume.
_identity_rule: Generate a SET of 3-5 canonical chest-up portraits per presenter — identical face and framing, varied outfit and setting — and reuse those approved files as input_image, rotating between them. Same outfit every video reads as fake; regenerating fresh every video lets the face drift until recognition breaks. A small approved set is the middle ground. Eyeball every render against the others before adding it to the set, and discard any where the face has shifted.

P1: zip-up over a tank, couch in evening lamp light
P2: plain worn gym tee, gym floor
P3: plain tee or hoodie, sitting in the driver seat of a parked car, daylight through the windscreen

_base_image_map: Each prompt carries a base_image id naming which approved portrait to use. FOX-n / PAGET-n / P3-n correspond to the numbered variations in _wardrobe_variety. Keep one saved file per id.
_lotus_notes: V2 is the approved canonical base. V1 (full-body, street, minimal grey) is superseded — keep it only as a reference for her overall look.
Body shape barely reads at chest-up framing. Do not spend generations tuning it for these videos.
_reference_standard: LOTUS-1 (lotus V2.png) is the quality bar for the other three: correct chest-up framing, eyes to lens, unstyled wardrobe, genuinely ordinary setting, real skin texture, properly exposed. Match it.
_voice_rule: One voice per presenter, permanently. Set ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID_P1 through _P4 in backend/.env. Never assign voices per prompt -- the same face with different voices across videos breaks recognition exactly as badly as changing the face. There is deliberately no shared fallback: a missing voice throws rather than silently using the wrong one.
